heroText: Munich is Bavaria's polished capital, balancing beer halls, art museums, royal squares and Alpine access. Start at Marienplatz, visit the Residenz or English Garden, then plan Oktoberfest around Theresienwiese if your dates match. Munich Airport is northeast of the city, with S-Bahn and airport buses into town.

areas.name: Altstadt
areas.text: Altstadt is best for first stays, with Marienplatz, beer halls, shopping and major sights close together.

areas.name: Maxvorstadt
areas.text: Maxvorstadt suits museum trips, university energy, cafes and access to the Pinakothek art galleries.

areas.name: Ludwigsvorstadt
areas.text: Ludwigsvorstadt is practical for the main station and Oktoberfest access, but choose streets carefully.

areas.name: Schwabing
areas.text: Schwabing has restaurants, nightlife and easy access to the English Garden north of the centre.

airports.name: Munich Airport (MUC)
airports.text: Munich Airport is northeast of the city and connects to central Munich by S-Bahn, Lufthansa Express Bus and taxis.

airportTransfer.distance: about 35 km northeast of the centre

stayOverview: Altstadt is easiest for a first visit, Maxvorstadt works for museums, Ludwigsvorstadt is practical for the station and Oktoberfest, and Schwabing suits restaurants, nightlife and English Garden access.
hotelIntro: Munich hotels get expensive during Oktoberfest and trade fairs. Book early, check U-Bahn access, and choose Ludwigsvorstadt only when station or Theresienwiese convenience outweighs atmosphere.
rentalCars: Do not rent for Munich itself; trains are better for Salzburg, Nuremberg and many Alpine day trips.

history.text: In the 1790s, Munich became the largest German city to remove its fortifications, starting in 1791 under Karl Theodor and Rumford.
After making an alliance with Napoleonic France, the city became the capital of the new Kingdom of Bavaria in 1806 with Elector Maximilian IV Joseph becoming its first king.
The first Munich railway station was built in 1839, with a line going to Augsburg in the west.
